components.name: Primary Action
components.description: The compact high-emphasis action used to move from explanation to a concrete project or resource.
components.css: .ds-button-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; min-height: 2.5rem; padding: 0.62rem 0.95rem; border: 1px solid rgba(79,151,233,0.2); border-radius: 999px; background: var(--planb-color-accent-strong, #082952); color: var(--planb-color-canvas, #fffefa); font: 800 0.82rem/1.2 Inter, Segoe UI, Arial, sans-serif; text-decoration: none; transition: background-color 160ms ease, transform 160ms ease; } .ds-button-primary:hover { background: var(--planb-color-accent, #4f97e9); transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-button-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--planb-color-neon-cyan, #23f5ff); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Commons Panel
components.description: The major section surface, identified by a short masked band of network energy.
components.html:
Our mandate

A city that can govern its digital future.

Public-interest technology begins with shared understanding.
components.css: .ds-panel { position: relative; overflow: hidden; max-width: 42rem; padding: 28px; border: 1px solid rgba(79,151,233,0.2); border-radius: 16px; background: linear-gradient(180deg,rgba(255,255,255,0.98),rgba(243,249,255,0.98)),#fcfcfc; color: #030b20; box-shadow: 0 18px 44px rgba(8,41,82,0.08),0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.84) inset; font-family: Inter, Segoe UI, Arial, sans-serif; } .ds-panel::before { content: ""; position: absolute; inset: 0 auto auto 0; width: 24rem; height: 0.75rem; background: linear-gradient(90deg,#ffb604,#ff5db1 28%,#7468ff 58%,#23f5ff); mask: linear-gradient(90deg,#000 0%,#000 80%,transparent); } .ds-panel h2 { margin: 0 0 0.75rem; color: #082952; font-size: 2rem; line-height: 1.12; } .ds-panel p { margin: 0; color: rgba(3,11,32,0.72); line-height: 1.6; } .ds-panel .ds-eyebrow { margin: 0 0 0.65rem; color: #082952; font-size: 0.82rem; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; }

components.name: Process Timeline
components.description: A compact rail for explaining civic experimentation as a sequence rather than a sales funnel.
components.html:
1. Learn

    Build common understanding

    Frame the public need before selecting a solution.

  2. Test

components.css: .ds-timeline { display: grid; gap: 0; margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; color: #030b20; font-family: Inter, Segoe UI, Arial, sans-serif; } .ds-timeline li { position: relative; display: grid; grid-template-columns: 5rem minmax(0,1fr); gap: 18px; padding: 0 0 28px; } .ds-timeline li::before { content: ""; position: absolute; inset: 0 auto 0 calc(5rem + 0.48rem); width: 1px; background: rgba(79,151,233,0.28); } .ds-timeline li::after { content: ""; position: absolute; top: 0.34rem; left: calc(5rem + 0.12rem); width: 0.76rem; height: 0.76rem; border-radius: 999px; background: linear-gradient(90deg,#ffb604,#ff5db1 28%,#7468ff 58%,#23f5ff); box-shadow: 0 0 0 5px rgba(79,151,233,0.12); } .ds-timeline li:last-child { padding-bottom: 0; } .ds-timeline li:last-child::before { display: none; } .ds-timeline strong { color: #082952; font-size: 0.84rem; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-timeline h3 { margin: 0 0 0.45rem; color: #082952; font-size: 1.2rem; } .ds-timeline p { margin: 0; color: rgba(3,11,32,0.72); line-height: 1.55; }

narrative.overview: This system should feel like technology that a city and its people can call their own: open, capable, curious, grounded, and collective. It combines the legibility and trust expected of public-interest work with the energy of a living hacker community. The light theme is the primary expression: an open white field, dark civic typography, and precise blue structure with small flashes of electric color. The system is lightly layered, gently rounded, and quietly tactile. It is not bunker-like, crypto-bro, bureaucratic, or promotional. Neon cyan, violet, and pink appear mainly as shared gradient energy, focus signals, and small marks; they do not compete as independent brand voices. Dark mode is a supported alternative for preference and context, not the default identity.
keyCharacteristics: White-first civic clarity with a fully supported dark alternative.
Strong navy typography, civic blue structure, and selective commons gold.
Electric gradient details used as connective tissue, never as visual noise.
Rounded, layered surfaces with restrained ambient lift.
Dense enough for serious information, open enough for curious newcomers.

rules.name: The White Commons Rule
rules.body: New surfaces begin in the light theme unless the host product or user preference explicitly selects dark mode.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: A composition may use navy and blue freely, but gold or the electric gradient carries the single exceptional signal; do not scatter both across every element.

rules.name: The Weight Before Ornament Rule
rules.body: Establish hierarchy through size, weight, spacing, and measure before adding gradient text or decorative effects.

rules.name: The Quiet Lift Rule
rules.body: Shadows explain grouping and state; they never create glossy product mockups or dramatic floating slabs.

dos: Do begin with Warm Canvas, Civic Ink, Lugano Night, and Civic Sky before reaching for additional color.
Do use the electric trio as a shared gradient, small focus signal, or connective mark.
Do keep hierarchy decisive with bold headings, measured prose, and compact labels.
Do preserve keyboard focus, reduced-motion behavior, responsive collapse, and explicit light/dark preference.
Do prototype accepted system changes on the foundation website, then upstream reusable decisions into the theme package.
donts: Don't use bunker language: avoid oppressive black slabs, military dashboards, terminal cosplay, or security-theater styling.
Don't imitate crypto-bro aesthetics with speculative glow, coin imagery, luxury gradients, or hype-driven calls to action.
Don't mimic bureaucracy with dense formality, anonymous institutional blue, rigid document chrome, or passive language.
Don't turn the system into marketing with oversized claims, ornamental statistics, or conversion-pattern clutter.
Don't let cyan, violet, pink, gold, coral, and blue all compete independently in one composition.
